title: Keritot 13
description: Rabbi Meir’s “toasted grain” read as a stringency, Ravnai’s rule for impure foods refuted, a baraita on immersing midway, a pregnant woman and a nursing mother, whether a woman’s milk is a “spring,” the priest who drinks wine before entering the Temple or teaching, and the mishna on one act of eating that brings four sin offerings and a guilt offering.
topics: ⏱️ Rabbi Meir’s “as though eating toasted grain” is a stringency: proven from “unless he expends”
🍞 Ravnai in Shmuel’s name on impure foods “even the entire day”, and the conclusive refutation
🛁 Why one who ate less than the measure may not immerse, a pregnant woman who eats little by little, and a mother nursing her child
🥛 Is a woman’s milk a “spring”? Rava’s two refutations, Rabbi Yoḥanan on the oven, and the nine liquids of a zav
🍷 “Drink no wine nor intoxicating drink”: the first tanna, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar
🙅 Rav Aḥa of Huzal’s vow and Rav Ashi: “Go now and come back tomorrow”
📚 What one who drank wine may not teach or rule on, and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
🧮 Mishna: one act of eating, four sin offerings and one guilt offering; Rabbi Meir adds Shabbat

a1.he: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְחוּמְרָא, הַיְינוּ דְקָתָנֵי: ״עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶא״, עַד דִּשְׁהִיָּ[ה] דִּילֵיהּ כְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.

a2.he: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְקוּלָּא, ״וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אִם שָׁהָה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינָּה: רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְחוּמְרָא? שְׁמַע מִינָּה.

a3.he: אָמַר רַבְנַאי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בַּחֲלָבִים וּבִנְבֵילָה עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶא מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס. אוֹכָלִים טְמֵאִים, שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים וּמַשְׁקִין – אֲפִילּוּ כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.

a4.he: מַאי קָאָמַר? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ, וְהוּא שֶׁאָכַל כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.

a5.he: מֵיתִיבִי: כׇּל הָאוֹכָלִין מִצְטָרְפִין לִפְסוֹל הַגְּוִיָּיה בְּכַחֲצִי פְרָס – מַאי לַָאו דְּאַכְלֵיהּ לַחֲצִי פְרָס בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס? לָא, דַּאֲכַל כְּזַיִת כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.

a6.he: מֵיתִיבִי: כׇּל הָאוֹכָלִין מִצְטָרְפִין לִפְסוֹל אֶת הַגְּוִיָּיה בְּכַחֲצִי פְרָס בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס, כֵּיצַד? אָכַל וְחָזַר וְאָכַל, אִם יֵשׁ מִתְּחִלַּת אֲכִילָה רִאשׁוֹנָה וְעַד סוֹף אֲכִילָה אַחֲרוֹנָה כְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס – מִצְטָרְפִין, יוֹתֵר מִכָּאן – אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין.

a7.he: לֹא הִתִּירוּ לֶאֱכוֹל פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר לֵירֵד וְלִטְבּוֹל, יָרַד וְטָבַל וְעָלָה וְהִשְׁלִימוֹ – מִצְטָרֵף. הִתִּירוּ לָהּ לָעוּבָּרָה לֶאֱכוֹל פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר, מִפְּנֵי הַסַּכָּנָה.

a8.he: כׇּל הַמַּשְׁקִין מִצְטָרְפִין לִפְסוֹל אֶת הַגְּוִיָּיה בִּרְבִיעִית בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס. כֵּיצַד? שָׁתָה וְחָזַר וְשָׁתָה, אִם יֵשׁ מִתְּחִלַּת שְׁתִיָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה וְעַד סוֹף שְׁתִיָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה כְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס – מִצְטָרְפִין, יוֹתֵר מִכָּאן – אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין.

a9.he: הִתִּירוּ לָהּ לְמַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת לְהָנִיק בְּנָהּ, וּבְנָהּ טָהוֹר.

a10.he: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת: אִם יֵשׁ מִתְּחִלַּת אֲכִילָה רִאשׁוֹנָה וְעַד סוֹף אֲכִילָה בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס – מִצְטָרֵף. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבְנַאי, תְּיוּבְתָּא.

a11.he: אָמַר מָר: לֹא הִתִּירוּ לוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר לֵירֵד וְלִטְבּוֹל. מַאי קָאָמַר?

a12.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, הָכִי קָאָמַר: אָכַל פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר – לֹא הִתִּירוּ לוֹ לֵירֵד וְלִטְבּוֹל, שֶׁאִם יָרַד וְטָבַל וְעָלָה וְהִשְׁלִימוֹ – מִצְטָרֵף. וְאָתֵי לְמֵימַר: אַהֲנִי לִי טְבִילָה קַמַּיְיתָא, וְאֵין יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין טְבִילָה אֶלָּא בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה.

a13.he: קָתָנֵי: הִתִּירוּ לָהּ לָעוּבָּרָה לֶאֱכוֹל פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר מִפְּנֵי הַסַּכָּנָה. מִפְּנֵי הַסַּכָּנָה אֲפִילּוּ טוּבָא נָמֵי תֵּיכוֹל! אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הָכִי קָתָנֵי: הִתִּירוּ לָהּ לָעוּבָּרָה פָּחוֹת מִכְּשִׁיעוּר, אֲפִילּוּ טוּבָא, מִפְּנֵי הַסַּכָּנָה.

a14.he: קָתָנֵי: הִתִּירוּ לְמַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת לְהָנִיק אֶת בְּנָהּ, וּבְנָהּ טָהוֹר – אַמַּאי טָהוֹר? כֵּיוָן דִּיינַק חָלָב אִיטַּמִּי לֵיהּ מֵחָלָב!

a15.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לָא אִיתַּכְשַׁר – נִתַּכְשַׁר בְּטִיפָּה מְלוּכְלֶכֶת עַל פִּי הַדַּד! אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: בִּתְקִיפָה אַחַת, לֹא הִנִּיחַ טִיפָּה מְלוּכְלֶכֶת עַל פִּי הַדַּד.

a16.he: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁתֵּי תְשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר: חֲדָא, דְּקָחָזֵינָא לְפוּמֵּיהּ דְּיָנוֹקָא דִּמְלֵא חָלָב! וְעוֹד, מְקוֹם חָלָב מַעְיָין הוּא.

a17.he: דְּקָתָנֵי: חֲלֵב אִשָּׁה מְטַמֵּא בֵּין לְרָצוֹן וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן, (בְּהֵמָה אֵינָהּ מְטַמֵּא אֶלָּא לְרָצוֹן.)

a18.he: מַאי לַָאו ״שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן״ – דְּלָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ, וְקָתָנֵי: ״מְטַמֵּא״?

a19.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דִּבְנָהּ טָהוֹר – דְּסָפֵק יָנַק כַּשִּׁיעוּר וְסָפֵק לֹא יָנַק, וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר יָנַק, סָפֵק יְנָקוֹ בַּאֲכִילַת פְּרָס, סְפֵק יְנָקוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.

a20.he: וּלְרָבָא, מְקוֹם חָלָב מַעְיָין הוּא, וְלֹא צָרִיךְ הֶכְשֵׁר?

a21.he: וְהָתְנַן: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנָּטַף חָלָב מִדַּדֶּיהָ וְנָפַל לַאֲוִיר תַּנּוּר – תַּנּוּר טָמֵא. וְקַשְׁיָא לַן: בְּמַאי אִיתַּכְשַׁר? וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּטִיפָּה מְלוּכְלֶכֶת עַל פִּי הַדַּד.

a22.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא, רָבָא לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְהָתַנְיָא: נִמְצֵאתָ אַתָּה אוֹמֵר, תִּשְׁעָה מַשְׁקִין בְּזוֹב: הַזֵּיעָה, וְלֵיחָה סְרוּחָה, וְרֶיעִי – טְהוֹרִין מִכְּלוּם. דִּמְעַת עֵינוֹ, וְדַם מַגֵּפָתוֹ,

b1.he: וַחֲלֵב אִשָּׁה – מְטַמְּאִין טוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין בִּרְבִיעִית. רוּקּוֹ, זוֹבוֹ, וּמֵימֵי רַגְלָיו – מְטַמְּאִין טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה, בְּכֹל שֶׁהוּא.

b2.he: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מְקוֹם חָלָב מְעַיֵּין [הוּא], חָלָב נָמֵי נְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה בְּכֹל שֶׁהוּא, כְּזוֹבוֹ וְרוּקּוֹ! אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מְקוֹם חֲלֵב אִשָּׁה לָאו מַעְיָין הוּא.

b3.he: אִי הָכִי, קַשְׁיָא הָא מַתְנִיתָא וְאָמַר רָבָא: ״מְטַמֵּא בֵּין לְרָצוֹן וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן״!

b4.he: מִי סָבְרַתְּ ״שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן״ דְּאָמַר – דְּלָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ? לָא, מַאי ״שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן״ דְּאָמַר, דְּדַעְתֵּיהּ דְּתִינוֹק קָרִיבָא לְגַבֵּי חָלָב, אֲבָל אָמַר לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ – טָהוֹר.

b5.he: אָכַל אוֹכָלִין טְמֵאִין וְכוּ׳. לְמָה לִי שְׁהִיָּיה, דְּקָתָנֵי: וְשָׁהָה? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, הָכִי קָתָנֵי: אָכַל אוֹכָלִין טְמֵאִין, וְשָׁתָה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין, וְשָׁתָה רְבִיעִית יַיִן, וְשָׁהָה בַּאֲכִילָתָן וּבִשְׁתִיָּיתָן כְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס, וְנִכְנַס לַמִּקְדָּשׁ – חַיָּיב.

b6.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״יַיִן וְשֵׁכָר אַל תֵּשְׁתְּ״ – יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ כֹּל שֶׁהוּא, אֲפִילּוּ מִגִּתּוֹ?

b7.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְשֵׁכָר״ – אֵין אָסוּר אֶלָּא כְּדֵי לְשַׁכֵּר, וְכַמָּה כְּדֵי לְשַׁכֵּר? רְבִיעִית יַיִן בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם.

b8.he: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״יַיִן״? לוֹמַר לְךָ שֶׁמּוּזְהָרִין עָלָיו כֹּל שֶׁהוּא, וּמוּזְהָרִין עָלָיו מִגִּתּוֹ.

b9.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״יַיִן״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא יַיִן, שְׁאָר מְשַׁכְּרִין מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְשֵׁכָר״. אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״יַיִן״? עַל הַיַּיִן – בְּמִיתָה, וְעַל שְׁאָר מַשְׁקִין – בְּאַזְהָרָה.

b10.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: ״יַיִן אַל תֵּשְׁתְּ וְשֵׁכָר״ – אַל תִּשְׁתֵּהוּ כְּדֶרֶךְ שִׁכְרוּתוֹ, הָא אִם הִפְסִיק בּוֹ, אוֹ נָתַן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם כֹּל שֶׁהוּא – פָּטוּר.

b11.he: בְּמַאי פְלִיגִי? תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: גָּמְרִינַן ״שֵׁכָר״ ״שֵׁכָר״ מִנָּזִיר.

b12.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא יָלֵיף ״שֵׁכָר״ ״שֵׁכָר״ מִנָּזִיר. וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר: מַאי ״שֵׁכָר״? מִידֵּי דְּהוּא מְשַׁכֵּר.

b13.he: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא: אָכַל דְּבֵילָה קְעִילִית, וְשָׁתָה דְּבַשׁ אוֹ חָלָב, וְנִכְנַס לַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְשִׁימֵּשׁ – לוֹקֶה, כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אֲחוֹתַאי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר. וְקָרֵי רַב עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: ״טוּבְיָנָא דְּחַכִּימֵי״.

b14.he: רַב אַחָא דְּהוּצָל הֲוָה נִידְרָא עֲלַהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ, אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל הָאִידָּנָא וְתָא לִמְחַר, דְּרַב לָא מוֹקֵי אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ מִיּוֹמָא טָבָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם שִׁכְרוּת.

b15.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, וְהָאָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וּמָר הוּא דְּקָא רָמֵי בֵּיהּ מַיָּא! אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בִּרְבִיעִית, הָא בְּיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי רְבִיעִית.

b16.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וּלְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבֵין הַחוֹל״ – אֵלּוּ דָּמִין וַעֲרָכִין, חֲרָמִין וְהֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת.

b17.he: ״בֵּין הַטָּמֵא וּבֵין הַטָּהוֹר״ – אֵלּוּ טְמָאוֹת וּטְהָרוֹת. ״וּלְהוֹרוֹת״ – זוֹ הוֹרָאָה. ״אֵת כׇּל הַחוּקִּים״ – אֵלּוּ מִדְרָשׁוֹת. ״אֲשֶׁר דְּבַר ה׳״ – זוֹ הֲלָכָה. ״בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה״ – זֶה תַּלְמוּד.

b18.he: יָכוֹל אַף הַמִּשְׁנָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּלְהוֹרוֹת״. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל אַף תַּלְמוּד? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וּלְהוֹרוֹת״.

b19.he: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא: יָצָא שֶׁרֶץ טָמֵא, וּצְפַרְדֵּעַ טָהוֹר, שֶׁשְּׁתוּיֵי יַיִן מוֹרִין בָּהֶן הוֹרָאָה. נֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וְלָא רַבָּנַן? – אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּזִיל קְרִי בֵּי רַב הוּא.

b20.he: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וְהָא רַב לָא מוֹקֵים אָמוֹרָא מִיּוֹמָא טָבָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם שִׁכְרוּת! שָׁאנֵי רַב, דְּאוֹרִי מוֹרֵי. וְנֹיקֵם (דְּלָא) [וְלָא] לוֹרֵי! – כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּיָתֵיב רַב לָא סַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּלָא הוֹרָאָה.

b21.he: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ אוֹכֵל אֲכִילָה אַחַת וְחַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ אַרְבָּעָה חַטָּאוֹת וְאָשָׁם אֶחָד: טָמֵא שֶׁאָכַל חֵלֶב, וְהָיָה נוֹתָר מִן הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.

b22.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה שַׁבָּת וְהוֹצִיאוֹ – חַיָּיב. אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵינוֹ מִן הַשֵּׁם.

messages.text: Continued from 12b: the Gemara asked whether Rabbi Meir’s ruling, that the time is calculated “as though he were eating toasted grain,” is a stringency or a leniency, and began to answer from the mishna: “And the Rabbis say: Unless he expends from beginning to end the time it takes to eat a half-loaf.”
Gemara

Granted, if you say that Rabbi Meir issued his ruling as a stringency, and that one is liable even if he ate the olive-bulk over a long period of time, this is the reason that the tanna teaches that the Rabbis say: Unless the amount of time he expends, meaning: Unless his expenditure of time is no more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is exempt.

notes.he: דאפילו ביותר מכדי אכילת פרס מחייב היינו דקאמרי ליה רבנן לעולם אינו חייב ביותר מכדי אכילת פרס אלא עד שתהא שהיית אכילתן כשיעור פרס:
notes.en: Granted, [if you say] Rabbi Meir [spoke] as a stringency: that he deems one liable even in more than the time it takes to eat a peras [half-loaf]; this is why the Rabbis say to him: he is never liable in more than the time it takes to eat a peras, but only if his time spent eating them is the measure of a peras.

notes.dh: אי אמרת בשלמא ר' מאיר לחומרא
notes.he: קאמר דאפי' כל היום תימשך אכילתו חייב היינו דקא מהדרי ליה רבנן עד שישהא כדי אכילת פרס ותו לא:
notes.en: [An editor’s marker notes that what precedes belongs to 12b.] Granted, if you say Rabbi Meir [spoke] as a stringency: he says that even if his eating extends the entire day he is liable; this is why the Rabbis respond to him: unless he expends the time it takes to eat a peras, and no more.

messages.text: But if you say that Rabbi Meir issued his ruling as a leniency, meaning that if one interrupts in the middle of eating he is exempt, the tanna should have stated: And the Rabbis say: If he expended more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf, he is exempt, which would indicate that if he expended less than this amount of time he is liable, even if he interrupted his eating in the middle.

notes.dh: אלא אי אמרת ר' מאיר לקולא
notes.he: קאמר דאפילו בכדי אכילת פרס לא מצטרף אם הפסיק בינתיים ורבנן בעו לאחמורי מאי עד שישהא הכי מיבעי להו למימר אם שהה כדי אכילת פרס חייב ומשמע אע"ג דהפסיק:
notes.en: But if you say Rabbi Meir [spoke] as a leniency: he says that even within the time it takes to eat a peras it does not combine if he interrupted in between, and the Rabbis wish to be stringent; why [say] “unless he expends”? They should have said: If he expended the time it takes to eat a peras he is liable, which implies: even though he interrupted.

notes.he: דלקולא קאמר כיון דאיפסיק ביני ביני פטור אע"ג דלא שהה יותר מכדי אכילת פרס א"כ וחכמים אומרים אם שהה מיבעי ליה למיתנא דהיינו משמע אם שהה כדי אכילת פרס אע"ג דאיפסיק חייב:
notes.en: But if you say: that he says it as a leniency, that since he interrupted in between he is exempt even though he did not expend more than the time it takes to eat a peras, then it should have taught: “And the Rabbis say: If he expended,” which would imply: if he expended the time it takes to eat a peras, even though he interrupted, he is liable.

messages.text:
Rather, isn’t it correct to conclude from it that Rabbi Meir issued his ruling as a stringency?
Conclude from it that this is correct.

notes.he: אלא מדקתני וחכ"א עד שישהא ש"מ דלחומרא אמר ר' מאיר ש"מ:
notes.en: Rather, from the fact that it teaches “And the Rabbis say: Unless he expends,” conclude from it that Rabbi Meir spoke as a stringency; conclude from it.

messages.text: With regard to forbidden fats and with regard to an unslaughtered animal carcass, one is liable for eating an olive-bulk even with interruptions unless the time he expends from beginning to end is more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis in the mishna.

notes.he: אכל שני חצאי זיתי חלב או נבלה:
notes.en: With fats and with a carcass: he ate two half olive-bulks of forbidden fat or of an animal carcass.

notes.he: דשיעור כל אחד בכזית עד שישהא באכילתו כדי אכילת פרס ולא יותר:
notes.en: With fats and with a carcass: whose measure is an olive-bulk each, unless he expends on eating it the time it takes to eat a peras, and no more.

messages.text: If he ate impure foods in the volume of a quarter-loaf of bread, or he ate repugnant creatures or creeping animals, or drank a quarter-log of impure liquids, he becomes impure and may not partake of teruma, even if consumption extended for the entire day, provided that they are eaten within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread.

notes.he: שיעורן לפסול את הגוף בחצי פרס:
notes.en: Impure foods: their measure for disqualifying the body is a half-peras [the quarter-loaf of the translation].

notes.he: פוסלין את הגוף ברביעית:
notes.en: And impure liquids: disqualify the body with a quarter[-log].

notes.he: שהה באכילת חצי פרס ובלבד שיאכל כל זית וזית שבו בכדי שהיית אכילת פרס:
notes.en: Even the entire day: he took [that long] eating the half-peras, provided that he eats each olive-bulk of it within the time it takes to eat a peras.

notes.he: אבל אכל אוכלין טמאין שנגעו בשרץ או בזב דשיעור אכילתן לפסול גוייתו מתרומה הוי חצי פרס ושתה משקין טמאין דשיעור שתייתן לפסול ברביעית אפי' כל היום כולו בכדי אכילת פרס:
notes.en: But [if] he ate impure foods that touched a creeping animal or a zav, whose measure of eating to disqualify his body from teruma is a half-peras, or drank impure liquids, whose measure of drinking to disqualify is a quarter[-log]: even the entire day, within the time it takes to eat a peras.

messages.text: What is Shmuel saying?
messages.quote: even if consumption extended for the entire day, provided that they are eaten within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf

notes.he: אפילו כל היום כולו והדר אמר בכדי אכילת פרס ותו לא:
notes.en: What is he saying? “Even the entire day,” and then he says “within the time it takes to eat a peras” and no more.

messages.text: This is what he is saying: Even if he eats the quarter-loaf of food over the course of the entire day he becomes impure, but that is the halakha only where he ate each olive-bulk within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread.

notes.dh: והוא שאכל כזית בכדי אכילת פרס
notes.he: פי' שאכל כל זית וזית שבחצי פרס בכדי אכילת פרס אע"פ ששהה בין זית וזית ולא אמרי' חצי פרס דפסול גוייה הוי ככזית חלב ונבילה להצטרך לאכול כל החצי פרס בתוך אכילת פרס:
notes.en: And that he ate an olive-bulk within the time it takes to eat a peras: meaning that he ate each olive-bulk of the half-peras within the time it takes to eat a peras, even though he paused between one olive-bulk and the next. And we do not say that the half-peras that disqualifies the body is like the olive-bulk of forbidden fat or of a carcass, so that he would need to eat the whole half-peras within the time it takes to eat a peras.

notes.dh: הכי קאמר אפי' כל היום כולו
notes.he: משך באותו חצי פרס של אוכלין טמאין הוו אכילה:
notes.en: This is what he is saying: even the entire day: [if] he drew out [the eating of] that half-peras of impure foods, it counts as [one] eating,

notes.he: שיש באותו חצי פרס בכדי אכילת פרס ולא ישהה בו יותר:
notes.en: provided that he ate each olive-bulk of that half-peras within the time it takes to eat a peras, and did not spend longer over it.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:
All impure foods combine together to disqualify one’s body from eating teruma if he ate a quarter-loaf of the impure food.
What, is this not referring to a case where he ate the quarter-loaf within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread?

notes.he: כוליה בכדי אכילת פרס ותיובתיה דרב פפא דמתרץ לדברי רבנאי:
notes.en: What, is it not that he ate the half-peras: all of it within the time it takes to eat a peras? And [this would be] a refutation of Rav Pappa, who explains Ravnai’s statement.

messages.text: No, it is referring to a case where he ate each olive-bulk within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, but he ate the full quarter-loaf in longer than that amount of time.

notes.he: לא דאכל כל זית וזית שיש בו בכדי אכילת פרס:
notes.en: No, where he ate each olive-bulk of it within the time it takes to eat a peras.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection from another baraita:
All impure foods combine to disqualify one’s body from eating teruma if he ate a quarter-loaf of the impure food within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread.

How so? In a case where he ate and then ate again, if from the beginning of the first period of eating until the end of the last period of eating there is no more than the amount of time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, they combine together. If the time spent eating is more than that, they do not combine together.

The Sages did not permit one who ate less than the minimum measure of impure foods, i.e., a quarter-loaf, to descend and to immerse in a ritual bath. If he descended, immersed, ascended, and then ate more impure food and thereby completed consumption of the full measure of a quarter-loaf, this second act combines with his previous consumption of impure food and renders the person unfit to consume teruma, despite the immersion in the interim.

notes.dh: לא התירו לאוכל פחות מכשיעור לירד ולטבול
notes.he: הואיל ואינו צריך לטבילה ולקמן מפרש מאי איכפת ליה:
notes.en: They did not permit one who eats less than the measure to descend and immerse: since he does not need immersion; and below [the Gemara] explains why it should matter to him.

messages.text: The Sages permitted a pregnant woman to eat less than the minimum measure due to the danger of her miscarrying.

notes.he: מפרש לקמן:
notes.en: They permitted her, etc.: this is explained below.

notes.dh: התירו לעוברה לאכול פחות מכשיעור מפני הסכנה
notes.he: ואם תאמר אפילו בלא סכנה נמי כדאמרינן (טהרות פ"ב מ"ג) והשלישי יאכל בנזיד הדמע וכן פרק קמא דחולין (דף ב:) קאמר טמא בחולין מאי למימרא ואף על גב שחולין טמאין וי"ל הכא מיירי לענין לאכול תרומה אחר כך אבל בלא לאכול תרומה אפילו כשיעור נמי ואם תאמר מאי פריך מפני הסכנה אפילו טובא נמי ויש לומר דזימנין שאין לה כי אם תרומה:
notes.en: They permitted a pregnant woman to eat less than the measure due to the danger: And if you say: even without danger [it is permitted], as we say (Tohorot 2:3): “And the third[-degree] may be eaten in a stew of teruma mixture”; and likewise in the first chapter of Ḥullin (2b) it says: “An impure person [slaughtering] non-sacred food: what is the point of saying it?” even though the non-sacred food is [thereby] impure. One may say: here it deals with eating teruma afterward; but where she will not eat teruma, even the full measure [is permitted]. And if you say: what is [the Gemara’s] objection, “due to the danger, let her eat even a lot”? One may say: at times she has nothing but teruma.

notes.he: ואפי' לריש לקיש דחצי שיעור מותר מן התורה מדרבנן מיהו אסור ובמקום הסכנה התירו:
notes.en: Due to the danger: even according to Reish Lakish, [who holds] that a half-measure is permitted by Torah law, it is in any case forbidden by rabbinic law, and in a place of danger they permitted it.

messages.text: All impure liquids combine to disqualify one’s body from eating teruma if one consumes a quarter-log within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread.

How so? In a case where he drank and then drank again, and in total he drank a quarter-log, if from the beginning of the first act of drinking until the end of the last act of drinking there is no more than the amount of time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, they combine together. But if the period of drinking is more than that amount of time, they do not combine.

With regard to a woman who has the status of first-degree impurity because she came into contact with one who was impure with impurity imparted by a corpse, the Sages permitted her to nurse her child, and her child remains pure. If the child touches teruma he does not render it disqualified, despite having consumed milk that presumably became impure upon leaving the body of the mother.

notes.he: לאשה שנגעה בטמא מת:
notes.en: One who touched one impure through a corpse: [they permitted it] to a woman who touched one impure through a corpse.

notes.he: לא התירו לו לאוכל פחות מכשיעור כו' והתירו לה לעוברה כו' והתירו למגע טמא מת כו' כל הני מפרש לקמן:
notes.en: They did not permit one who eats less than the measure, etc., and they permitted a pregnant woman, etc., and they permitted one who touched one impure through a corpse, etc.: all of these it explains below.

messages.text: In any event, the baraita taught that if from the beginning of the first period of eating until the end of the last period of eating there is no more than the amount of time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, they combine together. This apparently contradicts the opinion of Ravnai, who says that if one eats a quarter-loaf of impure food in total and ate each olive-bulk within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, his acts of eating combine together and he is disqualified from consuming teruma.
messages.quote: if from the beginning of the first period of eating until the end of the last period of eating there is no more than the amount of time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, they combine together

messages.text: The refutation of the opinion of Ravnai is a conclusive refutation.
messages.quote: even if consumption extended for the entire day

notes.he: דאמר כל זית וזית כו':
notes.en: The refutation of Ravnai: who said: each olive-bulk, etc.

messages.text: § The Gemara further discusses the baraita. The Master said above: The Sages did not permit one who ate less than the minimum measure of impure foods, i.e., a quarter-loaf, to descend and to immerse in a ritual bath. What is he saying; why is this prohibited?
messages.quote: did not permit one who ate less than the minimum measure of impure foods to descend and to immerse

messages.text: This is what the tanna in the baraita is saying: If he ate less than the minimum measure that causes impurity, the Sages did not permit him to descend and immerse. As, if he would descend and immerse and ascend and eat more impure food and thereby complete the full measure of a quarter-loaf within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf, all the impure food he ate would combine together to disqualify him from eating teruma;

and yet he might come to say: My first immersion following my first consumption of impure food was effective for me, and no additional immersion is required now that I ate merely another half-measure of impure food. But in fact, he does not know that immersion is effective in purifying him only at the end, and that if he now makes contact with teruma he will render it disqualified. Therefore, the Sages prohibited immersion in such a case to prevent one from reaching this erroneous conclusion.

notes.dh: אמר מר לא התירו לאוכל כו'
notes.he: מאי קאמר הכי קאמר אכל פחות מכשיעור חצי שיעור של טומאה לא התירו לו לירד ולטבול כשאוכל אותו חצי שיעור מפני שאם ירד וטבל ועלה ואח"כ אכל חצי שיעור והשלימו לחצי שיעור ראשון מצטרפין אע"פ שטבל וחייב לטבול עכשיו ואם היו מתירין לו לטבול מיד כשאכל חצי שיעור ראשון כיון שטבל ועלה ושוב השלימו אתי למימר אהניא לי טבילה קמייתא שטבלתי בינתים דלא מצטרפי ואינו חייב עכשיו לטבול והוא אינו יודע שכיון שכשעלה השלימו לא עלתה לו טבילה ומצטרפי ואין טבילה אלא באחרונה דההיא טבילה אחרונה שאחר האיסור הויא עיקר:
notes.en: The Master said: They did not permit one who eats, etc. What is he saying? This is what he is saying: [if] he ate less than the measure, half the measure of impurity, they did not permit him to descend and immerse when he eats that half-measure. For if he descended and immersed and ascended, and afterward ate a half-measure and completed the first half-measure, they combine even though he immersed, and he must immerse now. And if they had permitted him to immerse immediately when he ate the first half-measure, then since he immersed and ascended and then completed it, he would come to say: My first immersion, which I performed in the interim, was effective for me, so they do not combine and I am not required to immerse now. And he does not know that since he completed it after he ascended, the immersion did not count for him and they combine; and immersion counts only at the end, for the last immersion, after the prohibition, is the essential one.

messages.text: It was taught that the Sages permitted a pregnant woman to eat less than the minimum measure due to the danger of her miscarrying. Under the assumption that she is permitted to eat only less than the measure but not a full measure: Since it is permitted for her due to the danger, let her even eat a lot, i.e., more than the measure.
messages.quote: permitted a pregnant woman to eat less than the minimum measure due to the danger

notes.he: התירו לעוברה שהריחה ביוה"כ לאכל פחות פחות מכשיעור כותבת מפני הסכנה שלא תפיל:
notes.en: They permitted a pregnant woman who smelled [food] on Yom Kippur to eat little by little, less than the measure of a date, due to the danger that she might miscarry.

notes.he: יותר מכשיעור תיכול עד שתשוב נפשה:
notes.en: Even a lot: let her eat more than the measure, until she is revived.

messages.text: This is what the baraita is teaching: They permitted a pregnant woman to eat less than the measure of an olive-bulk within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, even if she ultimately eats a lot in this manner, due to the danger of her miscarrying.

notes.he: פחות פחות מכשיעור תאכל בכל פעם ואפי' טובא דמצוה לשנות שלא תאכל שיעור שלם ביחד:
notes.en: Rav Pappa said: This is what it teaches: she should eat less than the measure each time, little by little, even a lot, for it is a mitzva to alter [the manner of eating] so that she does not eat a full measure at once.

messages.text: It was taught that with regard to a woman who came in contact with one who was impure due to a corpse, the Sages permitted her to nurse her child, and her child remains pure and may therefore be fed teruma. Why is he pure? Once he nurses from the milk of his mother, he becomes impure from the milk.
messages.quote: permitted her to nurse her child, and her child remains pure

notes.he: דבשלמא ממגע שנגע בה לא מיטמא בנה שהיא שנגעה בטמא מת הויא ראשונה ואין אדם וכלים מטמאין אלא מאב הטומאה אלא מחלב איטמי דהאוכל כחצי פרס אוכלין טמאין נפסל גופו:
notes.en: He becomes impure from the milk: for granted, from the contact, when she touched him, her son does not become impure, since she, having touched one impure through a corpse, is first-degree, and people and vessels become impure only from a primary source of impurity. Rather, he becomes impure from the milk, for one who eats a half-peras of impure foods, his body is disqualified.

notes.dh: כיון דינק לה מחלב איטמי ליה מחלב כו'
notes.he: הא איתכשרת בטיפה מלוכלכת על פי הדד שאותה טיפה אין סופה שיניקנה התינוק והוא משקה ואם תאמר והא אמר פרק כל שעה (פסחים דף לג:) מכי סחט לה בצר שיעוריה ופירש הר"י לענין הכשר דפחות מכשיעור לא מקבל הכשר והכא בפה התינוק אין חלב כביצה ויש לומר דמדרבנן לא בעי כביצה והתם היינו דאורייתא:
notes.en: Since he nursed, he became impure from the milk, etc.: [for] it was rendered susceptible by the drop smeared on the nipple, since that drop is not destined to be nursed by the infant, and it is a liquid. And if you say: but it says in the chapter Kol Sha’a (Pesaḥim 33b): “Once he squeezed it, its measure decreased,” and the Ri explained [it as] referring to rendering susceptible, that less than the measure does not receive susceptibility; and here, in the infant’s mouth, there is not an egg-bulk of milk. One may say: by rabbinic law it does not require an egg-bulk, and there it is by Torah law.

notes.he: כיון דינק מחלב איטמי ליה מחלב ונפסל גופו מטומאת גוייה:
notes.en: Why is her son pure: since he nursed of the milk, he became impure from the milk and his body is disqualified through the impurity of the body.

notes.he: לאשה שנגעה בטמא מת דהויא ולד ראשון להניק את בנה ובנה טהור דאינו מטמא לא קדש ולא תרומה בנגיעה מ"ט היא לא מטמיא ליה לבנה בנגיעה דאיהי הויא ולד טומאה ואין ולד טומאה מטמא אדם ולא חלב שלה אינו מטמא אותו דאע"ג דמשקה הוא כיון דהיינו מאכל של תינוק אמרינן משקה הבא לאוכל כאוכל דמי כדתנן חולב אדם בי"ט לתוך הקדירה אבל לא לתוך הקערה דקדרה עושין בה אוכל ואמרי' משקה הבא לאוכל אוכל הוא וכאוכלא דאיפרת דמי אבל לא לתוך הקערה דקערה היינו כעין כוס ופעמים משימין בה משקין הלכך אין חולב בה דהוי נולד:
notes.en: It teaches: they permitted one who touched one impure through a corpse: a woman who touched one impure through a corpse, who is a first-degree derivative, [they permitted] to nurse her son, and her son is pure, so that he does not render sacred food or teruma impure by touching. What is the reason? She does not render her son impure by touching, since she is a derivative of impurity, and a derivative of impurity does not render a person impure. And her milk does not render him impure either, for even though it is a liquid, since it is an infant’s food we say: a liquid that comes [to be used] as food is like food, as we learned: One may milk [an animal] on a Festival into a pot, but not into a bowl; for in a pot one makes food, and we say a liquid that comes [to be used] as food is food, like food that was separated [from its source]; but not into a bowl, for a bowl is like a cup, and sometimes liquids are put in it; therefore one may not milk into it, for [the milk] would be newly created [nolad].

notes.he: וקא בעי בנה אמאי טהור כיון דינק חלב איטמי ליה מחלב דהיינו אוכלין טמאין:
notes.en: And [the Gemara] asks: why is her son pure? Since he nursed milk, he became impure from the milk, for that is impure food.

messages.text: And if you would say that the mother’s milk was not rendered susceptible to impurity because it never came into contact with a liquid, which is necessary in order to render a food item susceptible to impurity, that is not so, as it is rendered susceptible to ritual impurity due to the drop of milk that is smeared on the nipple. Since this drop is not consumed by the child, it attains the status of a liquid rather than a food, and it subsequently renders the rest of the milk that passes through the nipple susceptible to impurity.

notes.he: האי חלב ולאו טמא הוא דחלב אין בו תורת משקה דמשקה הבא לאוכל כאוכל דמי במסכת שבת בפרק חבית שנשברה (דף קמד:) הלכך בעי הכשר:
notes.en: And if you say it was not rendered susceptible: this milk, and so it is not impure; for milk does not have the status of a liquid, since a liquid that comes [to be used] as food is like food, [as stated] in tractate Shabbat, in the chapter Ḥavit Shenishbera (144b); therefore it needs to be rendered susceptible.

notes.dh: הא איתכשר בטיפה המלוכלכת על פי הדד
notes.he: כלומר בטפה שפי הדד מלוכלך בו דההיא ודאי מכשר לשאר החלב היוצא דרך שם דהא לא קיימא לאכילת תינוק:
notes.en: But it was rendered susceptible by the drop smeared on the nipple: that is, by the drop with which the nipple is smeared, for that certainly renders susceptible the rest of the milk that comes out that way, since it does not stand to be eaten by the infant.

notes.he: האי חלב דכולו בא לאוכל ואין אוכל מטמא אדם אלא על יד הכשר:
notes.en: And if you say it was not rendered susceptible: this milk, which comes entirely [to be used] as food, and food renders a person impure only by way of being rendered susceptible,

notes.he: ניתכשר בטיפה מלוכלכת שעל פי הדד (שנזרעת) חלב ראשונה שמוצץ הילד אינה נעקרת כולה מן הדד אלא משתייר ממנה על פי הדד ומתוך אותה טיפה יונק התינוק שאר כל החלב וכשפוסק מלינק משתיירת אותה טיפה על פי הדד וליתכשר שאר החלב שהוא אוכל מחמת אותה טיפה מלוכלך שאינה אוכל וליטמא החלב וליטמא התינוק ואמאי בנה טהור:
notes.en: let it be rendered susceptible by the drop smeared on the nipple: [a word in parentheses in the printed text is unclear here] the first milk that the child sucks is not entirely drawn from the nipple, but some of it remains on the nipple, and through that drop the infant nurses all the rest of the milk; and when he stops nursing, that drop remains on the nipple. So let the rest of the milk, which is food, be rendered susceptible by that smeared drop, which is not food, and let the milk be impure and the infant be impure; so why is her son pure?

messages.text: The baraita is referring to a case where the child nursed with one strong suck, and therefore it did not leave a drop of milk smeared on the nipple.

notes.he: בכח:
notes.en: That he nursed with one strong [suck]: with force.

notes.dh: אמר רב נחמן כגון שינק התינוק בתקיפה אחת
notes.he: במציצה אחת בכח ולא הניח טיפה מלוכלכת שינק הכל ולא נתכשר החלב באותה טיפה הלכך בנה טהור:
notes.en: Rav Naḥman said: For example, where the infant nursed with one strong [suck]: with one forceful suck, and did not leave a smeared drop, for he nursed it all, and the milk was not rendered susceptible by that drop; therefore her son is pure.

messages.text: There are two refutations of this statement: One is that we see that the mouth of the infant is filled with milk, which means that it is impossible for it to have sucked so powerfully that it immediately swallowed all the milk without leaving a drop on the nipple.

notes.he: הלכך אי אפשר שלא תהא טיפה מלוכלכת על הדד:
notes.en: The mouth of the infant that is full of milk: therefore it is impossible that there not be a drop smeared on the nipple.

notes.he: שתי תשובות בדבר חדא דקא חזינן פומיה דינוקא דמלי חלב כשפוסק מלינק אלמא לא אפשר למיהוי בתקיפה אחת שלא ישתייר ממנו טיפה על פי הדד ומאותה [טיפה] מוכשר החלב וטמא החלב והילד:
notes.en: There are two refutations of the matter: one, that we see the infant’s mouth full of milk when he stops nursing; evidently it is impossible for it to be with one strong suck such that no drop remains on the nipple, and through that [drop] the milk is rendered susceptible, and the milk and the child are impure.

messages.text: And furthermore, the mother’s milk does not need to be rendered susceptible to impurity like other foods in order to become impure and transmit impurity. This is because the location from which the milk emerges is a spring, i.e., it has the same status as the woman’s body. Therefore, if the woman is impure, her milk is also impure.

notes.he: חלב לאו תורת אוכל [או משקה] אית ליה דאחד ממעייני האשה הוא כרוקה וכמימי רגליה דאמרינן לקמן דמטמאין טומאה חמורה בכל שהוא שהוא כאחד מאבריה:
notes.en: And furthermore: milk does not have the status of food [or of a liquid], for it is one of the woman’s springs, like her saliva and her urine, of which we say below that they impart severe impurity in any amount, since it is like one of her limbs.

notes.dh: אמר רבא שתי תשובות בדבר כו' ועוד מקום חלב מעיין הוא
notes.he: וכיון שמעיין הוא ומטמא כרוקה אין הדד שמשום שמיוחד לתינוק ליהוי אוכל וניטל שם משקה מיניה דאתי למימר דאינו מעיין ואינו מטמא בזבה כרוקה ואם כן למה צריך הכשר והשתא טעי רבא וסבר דכיון שהוא מעוגל ויוצא כרוק חשיב מעיין אף על גב דאינו חוזר ונבלע ומנלן לרבא דמעיין הוא דתנא חלב האשה מטמא לרצון ושלא לרצון א"כ משקה הוא מן התורה ומעיין הוי כזבה דאי לאו מעיין הוא לא הוה מטמא כ"א לרצון כמו חלב הבהמה ואע"ג דחמור מחלב הבהמה לענין דם מגפתה כדאיתא בסיפא דההיא משנה מ"מ אי לאו מעיין הוא לא הוה מטמא שלא לרצון שיטת הר"י אבל רש"י פירש מקום חלב מעיין הוא ולאו תורת אוכל אית ליה דאחד ממעייני אשה הוא כרוקה ומימי רגליה דאמר לקמן דמטמאין טומאה חמורה בכל שהוא כמו א' מאבריה וקשה שהרי הכא מיירי בטמא מת ואין לו מעיינות ותו מאי קאמר כאחד מאבריה והלא נדה עצמה אינה מטמאה לאבריה ותו דרוקה ומימי רגליה צריכי קרא ולא אתו מהאי סברא לכן נראה כמו שפירשתי:
notes.en: In brief: Rava said: There are two refutations…and furthermore, the place of the milk is a spring. Since it is a spring and imparts impurity like her saliva, we cannot say that the milk at the nipple, because it is designated for the infant, is food and loses the name “liquid,” for that would mean it is not a spring and does not impart impurity in a zava like her saliva; and if so [it is a spring], why does it need to be rendered susceptible? At this stage Rava mistakenly thinks that since it gathers and comes out like saliva it counts as a spring, even though it is not reabsorbed. Rava’s source is the mishna “a woman’s milk renders susceptible to satisfaction and not to satisfaction”: so it is a liquid by Torah law and a spring, like a zava’s; were it not a spring it would render susceptible only to satisfaction, like an animal’s milk; and even though it is more stringent than an animal’s milk with regard to the blood of its wound, as in the latter clause of that mishna, still, were it not a spring it would not render susceptible not to satisfaction. That is the approach of the Ri. Rashi explained that it is one of the woman’s springs, like her saliva and urine, which impart severe impurity in any amount, like one of her limbs. Tosafot find this difficult: here the case is a woman [impure through contact with] one impure through a corpse, who has no springs [of impurity]; what does “like one of her limbs” mean, when a menstruating woman herself does not impart impurity through her limbs; and her saliva and urine need a verse and do not come from this reasoning. Therefore it seems as Tosafot explained. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: מכאן דמשקין שיש תורת מעיין עליהם מכשירין אפי' שלא לרצון ואפי' באין מאדם טהור דהא בחלב אשה טהורה מיירי מתני' דומיא דחלב בהמה דבטמאה מאי איריא שיש עליו תורת מעיין כל משקין טמאין מכשירין כדתנן בטהרות וטעמא מתוך שמטמא שלא לרצון מכשירין נמי שלא לרצון מיהו נראה דוקא טמאין הבאין מגוף אבל משקין שנטמאו בשרץ דינן כמשקין טהורין:
notes.en: And furthermore, the place of the milk is a spring: from here [we learn] that liquids that have the status of a spring render susceptible even not to satisfaction, and even when they come from a pure person; for the mishna deals with the milk of a pure woman, parallel to an animal’s milk. For if [it dealt] with an impure woman, why specify that it has the status of a spring? All impure liquids render susceptible, as we learned in Tohorot. And the reason is: since it imparts impurity not to satisfaction, it also renders susceptible not to satisfaction. It seems, however, that this applies only to impure [liquids] that come from the body; but liquids that became impure through a creeping animal have the law of pure liquids.

notes.he: כלומר דלא חשבינן ליה כמכונס ביה ומפקד פקיד אלא מעיין הוא כאחד מאיבריה ומעיינותיה הוא כדאמר תשעה משקין בזב כו' וכיון דמעיין הוא ליטמא בנה. ומנלן דמעיין הוא דתנן חלב אשה מיטמא בין לרצון דניחא ליה לאשה דאחשביה ובין שלא לרצון אע"ג דלא ניחא ליה לאשה ולא לתינוק ביה וקתני מיטמא אלמא מעיין הוא ואמאי בנה טהור:
notes.en: And furthermore, the place of the milk is a spring: that is, we do not regard it as gathered in it and deposited there; rather it is a spring, like one of her limbs and her springs, as it says: nine liquids with regard to a zav, etc. And since it is a spring, let her son be impure. And from where do we [know] that it is a spring? For we learned: A woman’s milk imparts impurity whether to satisfaction, where the woman is agreeable, having given it importance, or not to satisfaction, even though neither the woman nor the infant is agreeable to it; and it teaches that it becomes impure. Evidently it is a spring; so why is her son pure?

messages.text: As a mishna (Makhshirin 6:8) teaches:

A woman’s milk renders food with which it comes into contact susceptible to impurity, whether it emerges to the satisfaction of the infant or not to its satisfaction. By contrast, the milk of an animal renders food susceptible to impurity only if it emerges to the satisfaction of the animal’s owner.

notes.he: של תינוק בין שלא לרצון שאינו רוצה להניק וקתני מטמא ואי הוה ליה תורת אוכל אמאי מטמא שלא לרצון הא לא איתכשר הכשר מעליא דדומיא דכי יתן בעינן דניחא ליה:
notes.en: Whether to the satisfaction: of the infant, or not to the satisfaction, when he does not want to nurse; and it teaches that it imparts impurity. And if it had the status of food, why does it impart impurity not to satisfaction? It has not been properly rendered susceptible, for we require [a case] like “if water be put” (Leviticus 11:38), where it is agreeable to him.

messages.text: What, is it not correct to say that when the mishna states that the milk emerged not to the satisfaction of the infant, it means that the milk is not amenable to him at that time, and yet the mishna teaches that it renders food susceptible to impurity?

notes.he: כלומר רואין אנו שפעמים אין תינוק יונק בכח ומניח טיפה מלוכלכת על פי הדד:
notes.en: [A marginal gloss (gilyon), printed with Rashi, begins here.] Rava said: There are two refutations of the matter, etc.: that is, we see that at times the infant does not nurse with force and leaves a drop smeared on the nipple.

notes.he: והרי הוא כאחד מאבריה ויטמא בלא הכשר כרוקה:
notes.en: And furthermore, the place of the milk is a spring: and so it is like one of her limbs, and it will become impure without being rendered susceptible, like her saliva.

messages.text: Since liquids generally render foods susceptible to impurity only if they come in contact with the food with the owner’s approval, it is clear that a woman’s milk has a different status than other foods or liquids. This means that it need not come into contact with a liquid in order to become impure or to impart impurity to another item. The question therefore remains: Why does the child remain pure when he drinks this impure liquid?

notes.he: מאי היא דלא ניחא ליה לתינוק הרי לא יתכשר החלב בטיפה המלוכלכת ע"פ הדד דשלא לרצון התינוק יצאת דדומיא דכי יתן בעינן וקתני מיטמא אף על גב דלא הוכשר אלמא מעיין הוא ואמאי בנה טהור:
notes.en: Not to the satisfaction: what is it? That it is not agreeable to the infant; then the milk is not rendered susceptible by the drop smeared on the nipple, since it came out not to the infant’s satisfaction, for we require [a case] like “if water be put”; and yet it teaches that it becomes impure, even though it was not rendered susceptible. Evidently it is a spring; so why is her son pure?

messages.text: This is the reason that her child remains pure: The reason is that it is uncertain whether it nursed the measure of milk necessary to disqualify it from consuming teruma, or whether it did not nurse a sufficient amount of milk.

notes.he: אלא מקום חלב לאו מקום מעיין הוא וצריך הכשר אבל לא ניחא ליה טהור דהא לא איתכשר ומהשתא יכול לתרוצי לה בשלא לרצון. ע"כ הגליון:
notes.en: Rather, Rava said, etc.: rather, the place of the milk is not a spring, and it needs to be rendered susceptible; but where it is not agreeable to him it is pure, since it was not rendered susceptible; and from now on he can explain it [the mishna] as referring to “not to the satisfaction.” Thus far the marginal gloss.

notes.he: רביעית ואם אוכל הוא חצי פרס ספק לא ינק כשיעור וטהור דהאי חלב אע"ג דמעיין הוא לא מטמא בכל שהוא דהא היא גופה לא מטמיא במגע דראשונה היא הלכך אין לחלבה אלא טומאת שאר משקין:
notes.en: The measure: a quarter[-log]; and if it is [counted as] food, a half-peras. It is uncertain whether he nursed the measure, and he is pure. For this milk, even though it is a spring, does not impart impurity in any amount, since she herself does not impart impurity by contact, as she is first-degree; therefore her milk has only the impurity of other liquids.

messages.text: And even if you say that it nursed a sufficient amount of milk, it is still uncertain whether it nursed the required amount of milk within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, or whether it nursed that amount in more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread and therefore is not disqualified from consuming teruma.

notes.he: דספק ספיקא היא דספק אם ינק כשיעור רביעית שמטמא או אפילו ינק רביעית ספק אם ינק אותו כשיעור כדי אכילת פרס וספק ביותר הלכך בנה טהור:
notes.en: This is the reason: for it is a double uncertainty: uncertain whether he nursed the measure of a quarter[-log], which imparts impurity; or, even if he nursed a quarter[-log], uncertain whether he nursed it within the time it takes to eat a peras or uncertain [whether] in more; therefore her son is pure.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Rava, is it correct that the location from which the milk emerges is considered like a spring, and therefore if the woman is impure the milk is also impure, and it does not need to be rendered susceptible to ritual impurity by contact with a liquid?
messages.quote: the location from which the milk emerges is a spring

messages.text: But didn’t we learn in a mishna (Kelim 8:11):
In the case of a menstruating woman who had milk dripping from her nipples, and it fell into the airspace of an oven, the oven becomes impure.

notes.he: כשהיא נדה. ואי מעיין הוא הא מיטמא בכל שהוא כאחד מאבריה והכשר למה ליה:
notes.en: The woman whose milk dripped, etc.: when she is menstruating. And if it is a spring, it becomes impure in any amount, like one of her limbs; so why does it need to be rendered susceptible?

messages.text: And this poses a difficulty for us: In what way was the milk rendered susceptible to impurity, such that it can become impure or render the oven impure?
It was rendered susceptible by the drop of milk smeared on the nipple.

notes.he: שהיא זבה ונטף חלב מדדיה ונפל לאויר תנור תנור טמא כלומר אוכלין שבתוכו טמא דחלב הוי אוכל ראשון ואוכל ראשון מטמא אוכל שני על ידי הכשר וקשיא לן במאי איתכשר וא"ר יוחנן בטיפה כו' אלמא לאו מעיין הוא וצריך הכשר:
notes.en: The woman: who is a zava [Rashi and the translation: a menstruating woman], and milk dripped from her nipples and fell into the airspace of an oven: the oven is impure, that is, the food inside it is impure, for the milk is first-degree food, and first-degree food renders second-degree food impure by way of being rendered susceptible. And it poses a difficulty for us: in what way was it rendered susceptible? And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: by the drop, etc. Evidently it is not a spring, and it needs to be rendered susceptible.

messages.text: Apparently, Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that a woman’s milk must be rendered susceptible in order to contract impurity.
And if you would say that Rava does not hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, as one amora is permitted to disagree with another, but isn’t it taught in a baraita:

notes.he: בהדיא דלאו מעיין הוא:
notes.en: And if you say, etc., but isn’t it taught: explicitly, that it is not a spring.

notes.dh: וכי תימא רבא לא סבירא ליה כר' יוחנן
notes.he: דאוכל הוא וצריך הכשר אלא מעיין הוא:
notes.en: And if you say Rava does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan: [who holds] that it is food and needs to be rendered susceptible; rather, it is a spring.

messages.text: You are found saying that there are nine liquids with regard to a zav: The sweat, ill-smelling pus, and liquid excrement are more pure than all of them, i.e., they do not become impure and do not render other items susceptible to impurity.

notes.he: קייטור"א בלע"ז:
notes.en: Ill-smelling pus: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: וליחה סרוחה. היינו מוסרחת שלו:
notes.en: But isn’t it taught: You are found saying, etc. And ill-smelling pus: that is, his putrid [discharge].

messages.text: The tears that emerge from his eye, and the blood that emerges from his wound,
and the milk of a woman who is a zava transmit impurity of liquids where there is a quarter-log. The saliva, gonorrhea-like discharge of a zav, and urine transmit severe impurity in any amount.

notes.he: דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:ח׳) וכי ירוק הזב בטהור וגו' וזובו ומי רגליו ילפינן מרוקו במסכת נדה בפרק דם הנדה (נדה דף נה.):
notes.en: His saliva, in any amount: as it is written: “And if the zav spits upon one who is pure” (Leviticus 15:8); and his discharge and his urine we derive from his saliva, in tractate Nidda, in the chapter Dam HaNidda (Nidda 55a).

notes.dh: וחלב האשה מטמא טומאת משקין ברביעית
notes.he: ואם תאמר כיון דמשקה הוי מן התורה כדמשמע בפרק דם הנדה (נדה נה:) דקאמר דמעות עינו דכתיב ותשקמו בדמעות שליש (תהילים פ׳:ו׳) וחלב דכתיב ותפתח את נאד החלב ותשקהו (שופטים ד׳:י״ט) א"כ ליטמא בכל שהוא כמו שאר משקין כדמשמע פר' קמא דפסחים (דף יד.) דקאמר (אי) דאיכא משקה בהדי בשר ואין רגילות שיהא רביעית מים נדבק בבשר וגם פרק קמא דהתם (דף יז:) קאמר משקה דמטבחייא דכן לא אמרן אלא ברביעית דחזי להטביל מחטין וצינורות אבל בציר מרביעית לא וגם בפ' אלו דברים (ברכות נב.) קאמר נוטלין לידים ואח"כ מוזגין הכוס שמא יטמאו המשקין שאחורי הכוס מחמת הידים ויחזרו ויטמאו הכוס ואין רגילות שיהא נדבק רביעית בדופני הכוס לכך נראה לומר שאין אלו רק מדרבנן ולכך בעי רביעית וקרא דקמייתי אסמכתא בעלמא:
notes.en: And a woman’s milk imparts the impurity of liquids with a quarter[-log]: And if you say: since it is a liquid by Torah law, as is implied in the chapter Dam HaNidda (Nidda 55b), which says [this of] the tears of his eye, as it is written: “And given them tears to drink in great measure” (Psalms 80:6), and of milk, as it is written: “And she opened the flask of milk and gave him drink” (Judges 4:19), then let it impart impurity in any amount, like other liquids. [That liquids impart impurity in any amount] is implied in the first chapter of Pesaḥim (14a), which says [the case is] where there is liquid with the meat, and it is not usual for a quarter[-log] of water to stick to meat; and also in the first chapter there (17b), which says of the liquids of the slaughterhouse: this was said only of a quarter[-log], which is fit for immersing needles and hooks, but not of less than a quarter[-log]; and also in the chapter Elu Devarim (Berakhot 52a), which says: one washes the hands and afterward mixes the cup, lest the liquids on the back of the cup become impure because of the hands and in turn render the cup impure, and it is not usual for a quarter[-log] to stick to the sides of a cup. Therefore it seems right to say that these are only rabbinic, and that is why a quarter[-log] is required, and the verse that is cited is a mere support.

notes.he: דבכל הנך ג' כתיב בהו משקה:
notes.en: [An editor’s marker notes that what precedes belongs to 13a.] Impart the impurity of liquids with a quarter[-log]: for with regard to all these three, [the word] “drink” [mashkeh] is written.

notes.he: במגע ובהיסט:
notes.en: Severe impurity: by contact and by carrying [hesset].

messages.caption: The nine liquids of a zav in the baraita: three pure, three that impart the impurity of liquids with a quarter-log, and three that impart severe impurity in any amount, with a woman’s milk in the middle group.

messages.text: And if you say in accordance with the opinion of Rava that the location from which the milk emerges is considered a spring, then milk also should transmit severe impurity in any amount, like the gonorrhea-like discharge of a zav and his saliva.
messages.quote: transmit severe impurity in any amount

notes.he: ואי אמרת חלב מעיין הוא כו':
notes.en: And if you say milk is a spring, etc.

messages.text: Rather, conclude from it that the location from which the milk of a woman emerges is not considered to be a spring, and the milk must be rendered susceptible to impurity in order to become impure or transmit impurity.

If so, this mishna in Makhshirin cited earlier (13a), which Rava said supports his opinion, is difficult, as it states that a woman’s milk renders food susceptible to impurity whether it emerged to the satisfaction of the infant or not to his satisfaction. The mishna is difficult, as food is generally rendered susceptible to impurity only when the liquid comes into contact with it to the owner’s satisfaction.
messages.quote: whether it emerges to the satisfaction of the infant or not to its satisfaction

notes.he: כיון דאמרת דלאו מעיין הוא קשיא הא דאמאי מטמא אפילו שלא לרצון:
notes.en: If so: since you say that it is not a spring, this is difficult: why does it impart impurity even not to satisfaction?

messages.text: Do you maintain that the term: Not to their satisfaction, that the mishna states, means that the emergence of the milk is not amenable to him? No; rather, what is the meaning of the expression: Not to his satisfaction, that the mishna states?

It means that the child did not indicate whether he desires the milk or not, but as a child’s mind is close to milk, i.e., he generally enjoys the milk, an explicit indication of interest or satisfaction is unnecessary in order for the milk to be susceptible to ritual impurity or to render other food items impure. But if he says, i.e., indicates, explictly that the milk is not amenable to him, then the milk is not susceptible to ritual impurity, and it remains pure.

notes.he: לעולם לאו מעיין הוא ומי סברת דהאי שלא לרצון דקאמר דאמר דלא ניחא ליה לא מאי שלא לרצון בסתמא ומשום הכי מטמא אפילו בסתם דלא אמר דניחא ליה דקי"ל דבסתם דעתיה קריבה גבי חלב הילכך מטמא אפי' בסתמא אבל אי חזינא דלא ניחא ביה לינוקא לא מיתכשר וטהור:
notes.en: Actually it is not a spring. And do you think that this “not to satisfaction” that it says means where he says he is not agreeable? No; what is “not to satisfaction”? Unspecified. And therefore it imparts impurity even when unspecified, where he did not say that he is agreeable to it, for we hold that when unspecified, his mind is close to the milk; therefore it imparts impurity even unspecified. But if we see that the infant is not agreeable to it, it is not rendered susceptible, and it is pure.

messages.text: The mishna teaches that if one ate one quarter-loaf of ritually impure foods or drank a quarter-log of ritually impure liquids, or if one drank a quarter-log of wine, and he entered the Temple and remained there for the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is liable. Why do I need him to remain in the Temple in order to be liable, such that it teaches: And remained there?

notes.he: (יב:) משמע במקדש שהה והיינו דקפריך בגמרא מה לי לישהויי דקתני ושהה:
notes.en: And remained the time it takes to eat a peras (12b): implies that he remained in the Temple; and that is what [the Gemara] asks in the Gemara: Why do I need him to remain, that it teaches “and remained”?

notes.he: פירש"י דלא קאי אנכנס למקדש דלא מחייב אביאת מקדש באכילת אוכלין טמאין אפי' נטמאו במת דאינן נעשין אבות הטומאה כיון דאין להם טהרה במקוה ונראה דאיירי באכל נבילת עוף טהור ושתה משקין טמאין כגון דם השרץ שמטמא כבשרו ונכנס למקדש:
notes.en: He ate impure foods, etc.: Rashi explained that this does not refer to “entered the Temple,” for one is not liable for entering the Temple because of eating impure foods, even if they became impure through a corpse, since they do not become primary sources of impurity, as they have no purification in a ritual bath. And it seems that it deals with one who ate the carcass of a kosher bird and drank impure liquids, such as the blood of a creeping animal, which imparts impurity like its flesh, and entered the Temple.

notes.dh: אבל אכל אוכלין טמאין ושתה משקין טמאין
notes.he: באוכלין שהן אב הטומאה קא מיירי דנגעי במת והיכי אשכחן דאוכלין הוו אב הטומאה כדאמר בפ' אור ארבעה עשר ובהנהו חייב כרת כשאכלן ונכנס למקדש אבל באוכלין טמאין בטומאה דרבנן לא הוי חייב כרת אלא לאו בעלמא:
notes.en: But [if] he ate impure foods and drank impure liquids: it speaks of foods that are a primary source of impurity, having touched a corpse; and where do we find foods that are a primary source of impurity? As it says in the chapter Or LeArba’a Asar. And for these one is liable to karet when he ate them and entered the Temple. [A printed editor’s note: It seems one should read: But [if] he ate impure foods, which is only rabbinic impurity, he is not liable to karet but [violates] a mere prohibition. But for foods impure by rabbinic impurity he is not liable to karet but [violates] a mere prohibition.]

notes.he: האי ושהה לא ידעינן אי שהה במקדש קאמר או שהה באכילתן:
notes.en: Entered the Temple and remained: this “and remained,” we do not know whether it says he remained in the Temple or remained in eating them.

notes.he: [נכנס למקדש ושהה] דמשמע דאנכנס למקדש קאי ושהה ושם אינו צריך שהייה כלום אלא מכיון שנכנס הרי הוא חייב דאפי' התם במסכת שבועות דקא בעי שהייה שיעור השתחויה הני מילי שניטמא בפנים בהיכל. אבל בשניטמא בחוץ לאלתר כשנכנס חייב:
notes.en: Why do I need remaining, that it teaches: [entered the Temple and remained], which implies that it refers to entering the Temple and remaining? But there he needs no remaining at all; rather, once he has entered he is liable. For even there, in tractate Shevuot, where it requires a stay of the measure of a prostration, that applies only where he became impure inside, in the Sanctuary; but where he became impure outside, he is liable immediately when he enters.

messages.text: This is what the mishna is teaching: In the case of one who ate a quarter-loaf of ritually impure foods or drank a quarter-log of impure liquids, or drank a quarter-log of wine, and remained involved in eating them or drinking them for no more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, and then entered the Temple, he is liable.

notes.he: פירוש ועבד עבודה אבל בכניסה בלא עבודה לא מחייב והכי פירשו בתורת כהנים:
notes.en: And entered the Temple: meaning, and performed the service; but for entering without service one is not liable; and so they explained in the Torat Kohanim.

notes.he: האי ושהה דקתני באכילתו קתני:
notes.en: Rav Yehuda said: this “and remained” that it teaches refers to his eating.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Elazar says: If one interrupted his drinking of the quarter-log of wine, or if he placed any amount of water into the wine, he is exempt.

notes.he: ר' אלעזר אמר אם הפסיק בה באותו רביעית שלא שתאן ביחד או אם נתן לתוכו מים כל שהוא ושתאו ונכנס פטור:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar says: if he interrupted in that quarter[-log], so that he did not drink it all at once, or if he put any amount of water into it and drank it and entered, he is exempt.

messages.text: When the Torah instructs Aaron the High Priest: “Drink no wine nor intoxicating drink, you, nor your sons with you, when you go into the Tent of Meeting, that you shall not die” (Leviticus 10:9), one might have thought that this applies even if he drank any amount, and even if he drank wine from its press, i.e., wine that has not finished fermenting.

verse.he: יַיִן וְשֵׁכָר אַל־תֵּשְׁתְּ ׀ אַתָּה ׀ וּבָנֶיךָ אִתָּךְ בְּבֹאֲכֶם אֶל־אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְלֹא תָמֻתוּ חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: Drink no wine or other intoxicant, you or your sons, when you enter the Tent of Meeting, that you may not die. This is a law for all time throughout the ages,

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “Nor intoxicating drink,” indicating that only the consumption of a quantity of wine sufficient to intoxicate is prohibited. And how much wine is sufficient to intoxicate? It is a minimum of a quarter-log of wine that is forty days old, which has already fermented.

notes.he: מתוק הוא ולא משכר:
notes.en: Until forty days: it is sweet and does not intoxicate.

messages.text: If so, why must the verse state “wine,” when the term “intoxicating drink” would have sufficed? It is to tell you that although one is not liable to receive death at the hand of Heaven for it, it is prohibited to drink any amount of it, even less than a quarter-log, and then enter the Temple; and similarly, it is prohibited to drink it from its press and then enter the Temple, and one who does so is liable to be flogged, as is the case with any other prohibition by Torah law.

notes.he: אבל אינו במיתה עד שישתה רביעית בן מ' יום:
notes.en: They are warned about it in any amount and from its press: but he is not [liable] to death until he drinks a quarter[-log] forty days old.

notes.he: והלא משכר נפקא לומר לך יין מגיתו ויין כל שהוא מוזהרין עליו לאו בעלמא ולא מיתה:
notes.en: If so, why does the verse state “wine”? Is it not derived from “intoxicating drink”? To tell you that wine from its press and wine in any amount, they are warned about it: an ordinary prohibition, and not death.

messages.text: From the word “wine” I have derived only that wine is forbidden; from where is it derived that other intoxicating beverages are forbidden as well? The verse states: “Nor intoxicating drink.”

If so, why must the verse state “wine”? This comes to teach that for entering the Temple after drinking wine one is liable to receive the punishment of death at the hand of Heaven, but for entering after drinking other intoxicating drinks, one violates only a regular prohibition.

notes.he: ויין נמי כדי שכרותו חייב עליו מיתה:
notes.en: And for other intoxicating drinks, a [mere] prohibition. And for wine, too, in the amount that intoxicates, one is liable to death.

messages.text: The verse is interpreted to mean: Wine you shall not drink, and intoxicating drink, meaning that you shall not drink it in the manner of its being intoxicating. But if one interrupted his drinking, or placed any amount of water into it and drank it, he is exempt.

With regard to what do they disagree? The first tanna holds: We learn by verbal analogy that the term “intoxicating drink” is referring to wine, from the term “intoxicating drink” mentioned with regard to a nazirite in the verse: “He shall abstain from wine and intoxicating drink” (Numbers 6:3). There it is referring only to wine (see Nazir 4a).

verse.he: מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר חֹמֶץ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ שֵׁכָר לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה וְכׇל־מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה וַעֲנָבִים לַחִים וִיבֵשִׁים לֹא יֹאכֵל׃
verse.en: they shall abstain from wine and any other intoxicant; they shall not drink vinegar of wine or of any other intoxicant, neither shall they drink anything in which grapes have been steeped, nor eat grapes fresh or dried.

notes.he: תנא קמא ור' יהודה:
notes.en: With regard to what do they disagree: the first tanna and Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: שכר שכר מנזיר:
notes.en: [We learn] “intoxicating drink,” “intoxicating drink” from a nazirite.

notes.he: גמרינן שכר שכר מנזיר דכתיב מיין ושכר יזיר מאי ושכר דנזיר ביין מיירי ולא בשאר משכרין:
notes.en: We derive “intoxicating drink,” “intoxicating drink” from a nazirite: as it is written: “He shall abstain from wine and intoxicating drink” (Numbers 6:3). What is “and intoxicating drink” of the nazirite? It speaks of wine and not of other intoxicating drinks.

messages.text: But Rabbi Yehuda does not derive that the term “intoxicating drink” refers only to wine by the verbal analogy from the term “intoxicating drink” stated with regard to a nazirite. Consequently, he interprets the word as referring to an intoxicating drink that is not wine.
And Rabbi Elazar holds: What is the meaning of the phrase: “Wine and intoxicating drink”? It is not referring to two separate items, but rather to wine in the manner that it intoxicates.

messages.caption: “Drink no wine nor intoxicating drink” (Leviticus 10:9): how the first tanna, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar read “intoxicating drink,” and what each makes of “wine.”

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is that which is taught in the following baraita:
One who ate a sweet dried fig from Ke’ila, or drank honey or milk, all of which can have an intoxicating effect, and he entered the Temple and performed the Temple service, he is flogged.

notes.he: מקום:
notes.en: A dried fig of Ke’ila [de’veila ke’ilit]: [Ke’ila is] a place.

notes.he: דאינו חייב אלא בשעת עבודה כדיליף לה בסיפיה מקידוש ידים ורגלים. בה"ג כהן ששתה יין ונשא כפיו פסול ושיעורו ברביעית כדאמרינן השותה רביעית יין אל יתפלל דתפלה בעי כוונה ומסתמא ברכת כהנים לא בעי כוונה טפי מתפלה:
notes.en: And entered the Temple and served: for he is liable only at the time of service, as it is derived at its end from the sanctification of the hands and feet. The Halakhot Gedolot [rules]: a priest who drank wine and lifted his hands [for the Priestly Blessing] is disqualified, and its measure is a quarter[-log], as we say: one who drank a quarter[-log] of wine should not pray; for prayer requires intention, and presumably the Priestly Blessing does not require more intention than prayer.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who maintains that any item which intoxicates is included in the prohibition.

notes.he: כר' יהודה דהא איהו אמר ועל שאר משכרין באזהרה:
notes.en: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, for he said: and for other intoxicating drinks, a prohibition.

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.
And Rav referred to Rabbi Elazar as the most gratified of the Sages, as the halakha is in accordance with his opinion.

notes.he: ואם תאמר והא אמר רב (כתובות דף י:) אכל תמרים אל יורה ויש לומר דהתם מדרבנן אבל מן התורה יין דוקא:
notes.en: Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer [so Tosafot’s heading; the daf reads Rabbi Elazar]: And if you say: but Rav said (Ketubot 10b): One who ate dates should not issue rulings? One may say: there it is by rabbinic law, but by Torah law it is wine specifically.

notes.he: מוטב שבחכמים והל' כמותו:
notes.en: Tuvyana deḥakhimei [“the most gratified of the Sages”]: the best among the Sages, and the halakha follows him.

messages.text: Rav Aḥa of the city of Huzal had taken a vow not to derive benefit from his wife. He came before Rav Ashi to request that he dissolve the vow.

notes.he: שלא ליהנות הימנה:
notes.en: Had a vow regarding his wife: not to derive benefit from her.

notes.he: לאחר אכילה ושתיה:
notes.en: He came before Rav Ashi: after eating and drinking.

notes.he: כדי להתיר לו נדרו ובי"ט היה:
notes.en: He came before Rav Ashi: to have his vow dissolved, and it was a Festival.

messages.text: Go now and come back tomorrow, as I have just drunk wine, and it is prohibited for me to issue a halakhic ruling, as Rav would not place a disseminator before him to communicate his lectures to the masses from the meal of one Festival day until the other, i.e., the next morning, due to drunkenness. Since it was customary to drink wine during Festival meals, Rav would not deliver public lectures on Festival days, as one who has consumed wine may not issue halakhic rulings.

notes.he: למידרש בפירקא:
notes.en: Would not place a disseminator over himself: to expound in the public lecture.

notes.he: מאחר שעשה שמחת יום טוב שאכל ושתה עד למחר משום שכרות:
notes.en: From one Festival day to the next: after he had held the Festival rejoicing, eating and drinking, until the next day, because of drunkenness.

notes.he: שלאחר אכילה בא לפניו:
notes.en: He said to him: Go now and come tomorrow: for he came before him after eating.

notes.he: לדרוש ולהורות בי"ט בצורך הלכתא די"ט שני משום שכרות שלא יטעה ומשום שכרות נמי לא רצה להתיר לו עד למחר:
notes.en: For Rav would not place a disseminator over himself: to expound and to rule on a Festival for the needs of the halakhot of the second Festival day, because of drunkenness, lest he err. And because of drunkenness, too, [Rav Ashi] did not wish to dissolve [the vow] for him until the next day.

messages.text: But doesn’t Rav say: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar that if one diluted the wine he drank with water and entered the Temple he is exempt; and the Master is one who puts water into his wine?
messages.quote: Go now and come back tomorrow

notes.he: א"ל רב אחא והאמר רב הלכה כר' אלעזר שאם נתן לתוכו מים כל שהן פטור דאינו משכר:
notes.en: Rav Aḥa said to him: But didn’t Rav say: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, that if he put any amount of water into it he is exempt, since it does not intoxicate?

messages.text: That is not difficult; that ruling of Rabbi Elazar applies in a case where one drank precisely a quarter-log of wine, whereas in this case I drank more than a quarter-log of wine. In such a case one does not maintain a clear mind even if he mixed in a small amount of water.
messages.quote: the Master is one who puts water into his wine

notes.he: אף על גב דרמא ביה מיא משכר ואנא יותר מרביעית שתאי:
notes.en: With more than a quarter[-log]: even though he puts water in it, it intoxicates; and I drank more than a quarter[-log].

notes.he: (בטעות) בשאינו שותה אלא רביעית ונותן בו מים כל שהוא אינו משכר הא אם יהא יותר מרביעית אע"פ שנתן בו מים כל שהוא אינו מפיג טעמו ומשכר ואני שתיתי יין יותר מרביעית:
notes.en: That is with a quarter[-log]: [the printed text has “in error” in parentheses here] where he drinks only a quarter[-log] and puts any amount of water into it, it does not intoxicate; but if it is more than a quarter[-log], even though he put any amount of water into it, it does not weaken its taste, and it intoxicates; and I drank more than a quarter[-log] of wine.

messages.text: § In the continuation of the passage in which the Torah prohibits a priest from entering the Temple after drinking wine, the verse states: “And that you may differentiate between the sacred and the common, and between the impure and the pure; and that you may instruct the children of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord has spoken to them by the hand of Moses” (Leviticus 10:10–11).

verse.he: וּלְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבֵין הַחֹל וּבֵין הַטָּמֵא וּבֵין הַטָּהוֹר׃ וּלְהוֹרֹת אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵת כׇּל־הַחֻקִּים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֲלֵיהֶם בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה׃ {פ}
verse.en: for you must distinguish between the sacred and the profane, and between the impure and the pure; and you must teach the Israelites all the laws that GOD has imparted to them through Moses.

notes.he: יין ושכר אל תשת בבואכם אל אהל מועד וגו' ולהבדיל וגו' ובבואכם להבדיל בין הקדש והחול נמי אל תשת יין ושכר:
notes.en: And that you may differentiate: “Drink no wine nor intoxicating drink…when you go into the Tent of Meeting…and that you may differentiate”: and when you come to differentiate between the sacred and the common, likewise do not drink wine and intoxicating drink.

notes.he: ולהבדיל דכתיב בתר יין ושכר אל תשת לימד דשתויי יין אל יורה:
notes.en: And that you may differentiate: which is written after “Drink no wine nor intoxicating drink,” teaches that one who has drunk wine should not issue rulings.

messages.text: The verse states: “And that you may differentiate between the sacred and the common.” These terms are referring to the halakhot of values and valuations, dedications and consecrations, and the verse is teaching that it is prohibited to issue a ruling concerning these matters after drinking wine.

notes.he: שאסורים שתויי יין לשום אותן לבעלים לפדותן דדילמא לא שיימי להו שפיר:
notes.en: Values and valuations and consecrations: that those who have drunk wine are forbidden to appraise them for the owners so that they can redeem them, lest they not appraise them properly.

notes.he: דהיינו דמים וערכין וחרמים והקדשות להורות באיזה ענין שאמר שיהיה קדש שאם אמרו בענין אחר חול:
notes.en: Between the sacred and the common: that is, values and valuations and dedications and consecrations: to rule in which manner he [must have] said it for it to be sacred, for if he said it in another manner it is common.

messages.text: “Between the impure and the pure”; these terms indicate that it is prohibited for one who drank wine to render decisions with regard to ritually impure items and ritually pure items. “And that you may instruct”; this is referring to issuing a ruling about what is permitted or prohibited.

notes.he: של איסור והיתר שתויי יין אסורין בה:
notes.en: The ruling: on what is forbidden and permitted; those who have drunk wine are forbidden [to give] it.

notes.he: של איסור והיתר:
notes.en: And that you may instruct, this is a ruling: on what is forbidden and permitted.

messages.text: “All the statutes”; this is referring to the halakhic expositions of the Torah. “Which the Lord has spoken”; this is referring to halakha transmitted orally to Moses from Sinai. “By the hand of Moses”; this is referring to the Talmud, the deliberations on the Oral Law, from which halakhic conclusions are derived. It is prohibited to teach any of these subjects after drinking wine.

notes.he: שדורשין בפירקא אסור לשתויי יין שיש בהן הוראה:
notes.en: Expositions: that are expounded in the public lecture; they are forbidden to those who have drunk wine, since they contain rulings.

notes.he: למשה מסיני:
notes.en: Halakha: [transmitted] to Moses from Sinai.

notes.he: שאם דורש בהגדה בפירוש מקראות לא יפרש ולא יורה בהן אם הוא שתויי:
notes.en: All the statutes, these are the exposition: that if he expounds aggada in the explanation of verses, he should not explain or rule on them if he has drunk.

notes.he: [משנה] שאפילו במשנה שסתומה אל יעסוק בם בשביל להורות:
notes.en: Which [the Lord] has spoken, this is halakha [Mishna]: that even with an unattributed mishna he should not engage in order to rule.

notes.he: ביד משה זה התלמוד ששם לא יעסוק כל עיקר שהתלמוד מפרש הכל:
notes.en: By the hand of Moses, this is the Talmud: in which he should not engage at all, for the Talmud explains everything.

messages.text: One might have thought that it is prohibited to teach even Mishna after drinking wine. Therefore, the verse states: “And that you may instruct,” indicating that the prohibition is limited to material that provides practical halakhic instruction, whereas one does not derive practical rulings from the Mishna.

notes.he: לאפוקי משנה שאין מורין הלכה מתוך משנה הלכך מותר לשתויי יין לשנות:
notes.en: The verse states: “And that you may instruct”: to exclude Mishna, since one does not rule on halakha from the Mishna; therefore those who have drunk wine are permitted to study it.

notes.he: לא יעסוק בה אפי' שלא יתכוין להורות:
notes.en: One might have thought even Mishna: he should not engage in it, even without intending to rule.

notes.he: לא אמר אלא בשונה בה ע"מ להורות:
notes.en: The verse states “and that you may instruct”: it said [this] only of one who studies it in order to rule.

messages.text: One might have thought that even teaching Talmud is prohibited. Therefore, the verse states: “And that you may instruct,” indicating that the prohibition is limited to issuing halakhic rulings, but it does not include teaching material such as Talmud, although halakhic conclusions may be derived from it.

notes.dh: ר' יוסי אומר יכול אפילו התלמוד
notes.he: יהא אסור ללמוד תלמוד לומר ולהורות לא אסרתי אלא הוראת הלכה למעשה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei [so Rashi’s heading; the daf reads Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda] says: One might have thought that even Talmud: would be forbidden to study; the verse states “and that you may instruct”: I forbade only ruling on halakha in practice.

notes.he: ור' יוסי אמר יכול אפי' תלמוד לא ישנה אפי' שלא יתכוין להורות:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yosei [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s heading] says: One might have thought that even Talmud he should not study, even without intending to rule.

notes.he: אינו אסור אלא ע"מ להורות:
notes.en: The verse states “and that you may instruct”: it is forbidden only in order to rule.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is that which is taught in a baraita:

The rulings that a carcass of a creeping animal is ritually impure and that a carcass of a frog is pure are excluded from this principle, as those who have drunk wine may issue a halakhic ruling about these matters.

notes.he: ששרץ טמא וצפרדע טהור ואין חוששין שהרי לכל גלוי:
notes.en: Those who have drunk wine may rule: that a creeping animal is impure and a frog pure, and we are not concerned, for it is known to all.

notes.he: ששתויי יין יכול להורות בו שהוא טמא. וכן צפרדע יכול להורות שהוא טהור הנוגע בו:
notes.en: Excluded is a creeping animal: that one who has drunk wine may rule on it that it is impure; and likewise on a frog he may rule that one who touches it is pure.

messages.text: Let us say that this is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who says it is permitted to teach Talmud, and these conclusions are obvious from the Talmud, and that it is not in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.

notes.dh: נימא רבי יוסי בר יהודה היא
notes.he: דאמר שתויי יין מותר בגמרא ואי אפשר שלא יבין ויורנו משם ולא רבנן דאסרו אפילו לשנות בגמרא וכל שכן שום הוראה:
notes.en: Let us say it is Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda [so Rashi’s heading]: who said that those who have drunk wine are permitted [to study] Talmud, and it is impossible that one will not understand and rule from it; and not the Rabbis, who forbade even studying Talmud, and all the more so any ruling.

notes.dh: נימא ר' יוסי בר' יהודה היא
notes.he: דשרי אפילו תלמוד ולא רבנן:
notes.en: Let us say it is Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda: who permits even Talmud, and not the Rabbis.

messages.text: You may even say that it is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and that this case is different, as it is a topic that one could go learn in a children’s school, and teaching is not considered issuing a halakhic ruling.

notes.he: היינו טעמא דמורין בהן דזיל קרי בי רב הוא דשרץ טמא הוא ולא צפרדע:
notes.en: You may even say the Rabbis: this is the reason that one may rule on them: for it is [a matter of] “go read it in the schoolhouse” that a creeping animal is impure and not a frog.

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, that it is permitted to teach material from which halakha may be derived, but it is prohibited to issue halakhic rulings.

notes.he: דבתלמוד מותרין לעסוק שתויי יין:
notes.en: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda: that those who have drunk wine are permitted to engage in Talmud.

messages.text: But Rav himself would not place a disseminator before him to communicate his lectures to the masses from the meal of one Festival day until the other, i.e., the next morning, due to drunkenness.
messages.quote: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda

notes.he: ואמאי לא דריש בפירקא כיון דגמרא שרי כל שכן מדרשות:
notes.en: But Rav would not place, etc.: and why would he not expound in the public lecture? Since Talmud is permitted, all the more so expositions.

notes.he: והא רב לא מוקים אמורא מי"ט לחבריה לפרש כלל בתלמוד משום שכרות:
notes.en: But Rav would not place a disseminator from one Festival day to the next to explain anything at all in Talmud, because of drunkenness.

messages.text: Rav is different, as he would issue halakhic rulings during his lectures.

notes.he: שהוא היה רגיל להורות לצבור ואם יפרש האמורא לפניו כלום בתלמוד אי אפשר שלא היה מורה:
notes.en: Rav is different, for he would issue rulings: for he was accustomed to rule for the public, and if the disseminator explained anything in Talmud before him, it would be impossible that he would not rule.

messages.text: And let him place a disseminator and deliver a lecture but not issue halakhic rulings.
Wherever Rav sits and delivers a lecture, it is not possible for him to do so without issuing a halakhic ruling.

notes.he: דכ"ע בעו מיניה:
notes.en: It is not possible without a ruling: for everyone asks him.

notes.he: כלומר יעמיד אמורא וישמור עצמו שלא יורה. דבר זה לא יתכן דכל היכא דיתיב רב מתקבצין לפניו אנשים הרבה ושואלין אותו באיסור והיתר ולא סגי ליה בלא הורה:
