notes.en: And let him place [a disseminator] and not rule: that is, let him place a disseminator and guard himself not to rule. This is not feasible, for wherever Rav sat, many people gathered before him and asked him about what is forbidden and permitted, and it was not possible for him without ruling.

messages.text: Mishna
There is a case where one can perform a single act of eating an olive-bulk of food and be liable to bring four sin offerings and one guilt offering for it.

notes.he: ואם תאמר אמאי לא חשיב ה' כגון נשבע שלא יאכלנו ואכלה ויש לומר מידי דאיתיה בשאלה לא קתני ומוקדשין דתני אף על גב דהוו בשאלה מכל מקום השתא שנשחטו ונזרקו דמן כהילכתא ליתא בשאלה אבל ליכא למימר דאיירי בבכור שהרי קאמר בגמרא אקדשיה מיגו דאיתוסף בה איסור וכו' ואי הוי מיירי בבכור לא הוה אומר אקדשיה שהרי קדוש בפטר רחם:
notes.en: Four sin offerings and one guilt offering: And if you say: why does it not count five, for example where he swore that he would not eat it and then ate it? One may say: it does not teach something that is subject to dissolution [by a sage]. And as for consecrated items, which it does teach even though they are subject to dissolution: in any case, now that they have been slaughtered and their blood sprinkled properly, they are no longer subject to dissolution. But one cannot say that it deals with a firstborn, for it says in the Gemara: “He consecrated it; since a prohibition was added,” etc.; and if it dealt with a firstborn it would not say “he consecrated it,” for it is sanctified by opening the womb.

messages.text: How so? This halakha applies to one who is ritually impure who ate forbidden fat, and it was left over from a consecrated offering after the time allotted for its consumption [notar], on Yom Kippur. He is liable to bring sin offerings for eating forbidden fat and notar, for eating the meat of an offering while impure, and for eating on Yom Kippur. He is also liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property.

notes.he: חד משום דאכל קדש בטומאה וחד משום חלב וחד משום נותר וחד משום יוה"כ:
notes.en: Mishna. Four sin offerings: one because he ate sacred [meat] while impure, one because of forbidden fat, one because of notar, and one because of Yom Kippur.

notes.he: מעילה:
notes.en: And a guilt offering: for misuse [of consecrated property].

notes.he: והא דחייב אשם מעילה אנותר אע"ג דלא שוה מידי ואמרינן בפרק כל שעה (דף כ"ט) האוכל חמץ הקדש במועד לא מעל התם בקדושת דמים דלא נחת עליו קדושת הגוף וכשנאסר בהנאה אינו ש"פ ולא נהנה מן ההקדש שוה פרוטה:
notes.en: And one guilt offering: as for the fact that he is liable to a guilt offering for misuse because of notar, even though it is worth nothing, while we say in the chapter Kol Sha’a (Pesaḥim 29a) that one who eats consecrated leavened bread during the Festival has not committed misuse: there it is a case of monetary sanctity, on which the sanctity of the body did not descend, and once it became forbidden for benefit it is not worth a peruta, and he did not benefit from consecrated property worth a peruta.

notes.he: אחד משום טמא שאכל קדש ואחד משום חלב ואחד משום נותר ואחד משום יוה"כ ואשם אחד משום זר שנהנה מן הקדש:
notes.en: Four sin offerings: one because of an impure person who ate sacred [food], one because of forbidden fat, one because of notar, and one because of Yom Kippur; and one guilt offering because of a non-priest [zar] who benefited from consecrated property.

messages.text: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out from a private domain to a public domain while eating it, he would be liable to bring an additional sin offering for performing prohibited labor on Shabbat.
That liability is not from the same type of prohibition, as it is not due to the act of eating, and therefore, it should not be counted.
messages.quote: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out

notes.he: דאין חיוב זה משום אכילה:
notes.en: It is not of the same category: for this liability is not because of eating.

notes.dh: ר' מאיר אומר אם היתה שבת
notes.he: כשאוכל והוציאו בפיו חייב חטאת משום שבת ואע"ג דאמרינן המוציא בפיו לאחר ידו ובמרפקו פטור שלא הוציא כדרך המוציאין הני מילי כי הוציא שאר חפציו בפיו. אבל אוכל כדרכו והוציאו בפיו חייב אמרו לו אינו מן השם דאינו משום שם אכילה אמר דחייב דהוצאה לאו אכילה הוא:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir says: If it was Shabbat: when he eats and carries it out in his mouth, he is liable to a sin offering because of Shabbat. And even though we say that one who carries out in his mouth, on the back of his hand or with his elbow is exempt, since he did not carry out in the manner of those who carry out, that applies when he carried out his other objects in his mouth; but food [is carried] in its normal manner, and [if] he carried it out in his mouth he is liable. They said to him: It is not of the same category: for it is not in the category of eating, [yet] he said that he is liable; for carrying out is not eating.

messages.text: Continues on 14a: the Gemara suggests that the mishna shows Rabbi Meir holds that a prohibition takes effect where another prohibition already exists, and answers that he holds so for a more inclusive or an expanded prohibition.
